Results per finding:

r1-27: partly fixed, partly already fixed.
- Already fixed in round 2: the discrete slots and the empty landside sector.
- Fixed now, glazed panes: t4 and t3 show a glazed pane in the lowest panel row of the two NE-flank slots next to the ribbon (bearings ~345 and ~13). t1 and t2 show none on the airside slots. Drawn in BT-02 B, tagged obs.
- Fixed now, flare shoulder: in t1 (near-orthographic, 0.073 m/px, 1.6 deg roll removed) the top rises 0.15 / 0.35 / 0.48 / 0.86 / 1.15 m above the corner at 0.2 / 0.5 / 1.1 / 3.4 / 6.6 m in from the limb. That is a rounded shoulder, not a vertical lip. The shoulder now appears in BT-02, BT-03 and BX-01; the spec stations 59.4 -> 60.9 are kept.

r1-28: already fixed. The round-2 helix (bearing 137 at the foot, 93 at the head) projects at 13.7 deg overall (11-18 deg locally) in view A, and at 14 deg from the t1 and t2 bearings. The photos give 15-16 deg. The head sits 2.8 m inside the silhouette from 126 deg, which matches t2.

r1-29: fixed.
- Masts: there are now 15 whips and 9 camera / lamp / bracket poles. t2 and t3 are taken from opposite sides with the camera ~12 deg below the rim, so each photo shows true heights only on its near half. I took near-side bearings as right + acos(a/0.92), with heights scaled from the rim widths (474 px in t2, 371 px in t3). Each photo's short far-side whips fall on the other photo's near set.
- 2015 lattice boom: rejected for drawing. It is a jib davit (post ~4.3 m, jib ~5 m) in t1, taken in May 2015 while the tower was still under construction. None of the 2025 photos show it. They show only a ~1.9 m post with a stay on the SW wing top (also visible in t5, 2018), and that post is drawn instead.

r1-30: two items rejected, two fixed.
- Rejected, louvred block: the tall dark louvred block beside the shaft (left of it in t1, right of it in t2 and t3) triangulates from the three photos to (-804.3, 259.4), with a residual of 1.3 m. I regenerated the sheets with `python3 tools/buildings/draw.py BI` (BI-01..04 plus the NAIP overlay) and looked at the PNGs. I cropped every changed view: the BI-02 west elevation, its right-hand labels and notes strip, BI-01 views 3/4 as vector and as NAIP overlay, the BI-01 table, all of BI-04, and the BI-03 long section. I also overlaid the traced pod outlines (imaged and relief-corrected) on NAIP crops to check the fit. I fixed the layout clashes I found: two leaders overlapping, level labels running into the notes strip, the box leader leaving its view, the BI-04 labels being cut off, and the glazing label overlapping the main-roof label. Then I re-rendered. I also confirmed that the spec_itb.json diff only adds content and that draw_data still loads it.

RESULT PER FINDING:

r1-26 FIXED. Before, BI-01 had only labels and no pod outlines. Now itb_pods.py traces all six pods on NAIP 2024. BA-A, from the ITB outwards: three D-shapes 55.9 / 51.6 / 55.9 m long, about 24.5 m wide, with the curved WNW edge scanned every metre. BA-G: three lenses cut off by straight end walls, 58.3 / 54.2 / 62.5 m long, about 25 m wide. The outlines are relief-corrected (frame model for BA-A, k(x) for BA-G) and drawn on BI-01 views 3/4. The overlay also shows the imaged trace, dotted. Heights come from the WNW dark band (visible face plus shadow) and are marked [obs, low]: BA-A rise 5.4-5.7 m, tops 23.3-23.6 m (range 21.8-25.0); BA-G rise 5.2-6.2 m, tops 22.2-23.2 m. The BA-A pod 1 DOF value of 25.9 m only meets the NAIP range at its upper end. Correction to the reviewer's evidence: photo a2 shows BA-A seen from the east, not BA-G. The pods have straight near walls and curved far rims, and the aircraft are seen tail-on at the ESE face.

r1-31 PARTLY ALREADY FIXED, REST NOW FIXED. Round 2 had already drawn the canopy line, the fritted wing bays against the clear central bay, and the lettering. What was missing were the canopy struts and their module. They are hanger pairs (one leg nearly vertical, one inclined) with a post under the canopy at each. I measured them on i4 as ratios to the 80-ft column bay: 0.493 (north wing) and 0.489 (south wing), so 40 ft. They sit 20 ft either side of every column line. Over the 180-ft centre section they stand at ±30 and ±90 ft, i.e. 60-ft spacing; the reviewer's 12 m figure holds only in the wings. The read positions fall within 0.5 m of that grid. The rhythm is recorded as obs-photo in spec facade.west.drawing_obs_canopy and in the README, and drawn on BI-02.

r2-26 FIXED. Each column head now branches into 5 members (a vertical post plus 2 per side): the count is [obs] from photos i3/i4, the geometry [inf]. The canopy struts are drawn as above.

r2-27 FIXED (the finding is valid). The raw NAIP eave stations fall steadily towards both tips. Median per bin, north/south: |u| 100-105 34.8/36.3, |u| 110-114 33.5/35.6, |u| 114-121 32.1/34.4-33.8. The photo silhouette in itb_photo_skyline.json also falls steadily; the south side rises 0.5-0.9 m only in the last ~2 m, at the fascia corner. So the fitted curve's rise from 34.40 (|u| 115-119) to 34.83 (|u| 123) is an end artefact of the even polynomial. The drawn eave now holds the fit's minimum from |u| 117 to the tip: tip 34.4 m (32-35.5) [obs, low]. The spec's 34.9 is a blend of NAIP 34.4 and photo 35.5. BI-01..03 are updated and the note is in roof.profile.drawing_note_tips.

r2-29 FIXED. New sheet BI-04 (A1), all heights [obs, low]. It contains:
- the BA-G NNE apron face and the BA-A ESE apron face at 1:750: pier bodies with the main-roof ranges, the pods, the end box, the BA-A pod 1 DOF point, and the BA-A glazed gate-room band (about 5.2-17.2 m AGL from photo a2; bay positions marked [unk]);
- sections through pod A1 and through pod G3 with the end box at 1:400;
- a pod table and notes.

r2-30 FIXED (identified; function inferred). On NAIP 2024-05-20, BA-G has exactly one rooftop structure higher than its pods: an 8 × 9 m box on the WNW end of pod G3, set back about 1 m from the pod end. Its WNW band splits into the box face (3.0 m) and the pod end wall (2.5 m), giving 7.4-10.3 m above the pod and a top of 30.5-33.4 m (26-37 with the main-roof range) [obs, low]. I checked all three G pods, the pier head, BA-F and the ITB north end and found nothing similar. This matches the cab in photo d2 (2018), a box with a dark window band and antennas on a raised roof volume. The old gate numbers 94/96 in d2 are BA-G numbering, so d2 shows BA-G. The function, a ramp-control cab, is [inf]: LiveATC lists 'Ramp G (West)' and there is no SFO source. The structure still stands in NAIP 2024. It is drawn on BI-01 view 4 and BI-04 views 1/4, and added to the spec as ba_g.pod3_end_box.
doubts: r2-30: I did not solve photo d2's camera position. Matching its cab to the NAIP box rests on that box being the only such structure on BA-G and on the heights being consistent (the cab sits about as high above the pod as the pod above the roof). The cab's function (ramp control) is inferred only.

All pod and box heights come from one NAIP image (half-level band widths) and are low confidence. The BA-G main roof is itself 13-20 m, which widens every BA-G top range. For BA-G pods the edges between the read apexes and end corners are parabolic [inf]. For BA-A pods the straight ESE side is only a weak brightness dip of about 8 grey levels.
BA-A pod tops read 21.8-25.0 m, a bit lower than the verification's 22.3-25.2 because a different half-level band definition was used; both are recorded.
The drawn tip height is now 34.4 m against the spec value 34.9 (a blend). I recorded this as a drawing note and did not change the spec value.

BX-01 (draw_compare) imports draw_itb.roof_line, so it will show the non-increasing tips when it is next regenerated. I did not regenerate BX-01. The modified BX-01 files in the working tree are not mine. Running draw.py also rewrites deviations.json, which showed no diff.

Per-finding results:

r1-23 (BA-B raised centre shown only at the south tip): VALID, FIXED by measurement. The new script dom_bab_band.py repeats both verification methods all along the pier.
- 2020 step shadow: the shadow of the raised roof on the lower ESE band is present at every 2-m station from t -1236 to -946. That is 290 m, from the bend towards T1 Center to about 20 m short of the tip.
  - Shadow length is 4.79-4.95 m (p10-p90 over 144 stations), so the step is the same ~5.9 m everywhere.
  - The imaged edge sits at s -387.8 with sd 0.13 m.
- 2020-2024 parallax: the centre moves 3.40 m (south) and 3.65 m (north), against 2.30 and 2.60 m at the outer lip, at every station where the images correlate.
- 2024 WNW edge: the raised roof's WNW wall shows as a dark band over the roof wells (t -1150..-960). That puts the lean-free edge at s -423.4; the south half's inferred -424.0 agrees within 0.6 m.
- Drawn result: hatched band with measured ESE edge s -391.0 (obs) and WNW edge s -423.4 (obs in the north, carried south as inf); raised part 32.4 m wide. BD-02 shows a 'typical' section with the measured widths 7.3 / 32.4 / 14.7 m and the step note.
- Stated as limits: the oblique north wing beyond the bend is not tested (unk). The 13.1 m outer roof is measured on the south half only, so the ~19 m top in the north is obs-low and depends on it.
- I checked the bend and the north end on 2020/2022/2024 crops.

r1-22 (BA-F octagonal hub, lantern, NW-arm monitor, hub section): ALREADY FIXED in round 2; refined here. BD-01 already had the octagon, lantern rings and monitor, and BD-02 view 1c already had the hub and NW-arm sections. I confirmed on NAIP crops that the monitor and rings sit where they are drawn. Refinements from dom_baf_hub.py:
- Hub outline and height: the four free hub faces (normals 73/163/208/253) put the roof edge on the SFO Museum octagon (offset -0.27 / +0.24 m). The fitted edge height is 12.1±1.3 m with an east-only lean and 10.4±2.5 m with the frame-model lean direction (obs, low). So the level-2 octagon is the roof outline. This band is now drawn and listed in the height table.
- Lantern: round 2 offered 'if concentric, a ~24 m top' as an inference. Being concentric would need about 11-12 m of rise. NAIP 2020 shows the ring casting a dark run of only 5.25 m or less to the east, which limits the rise to 4.6 m or less. The ring is therefore drawn off-centre, about 3.3 m east of the hub centre (inf), with the rise placeholder at that limit (unk). This correction to the earlier inference is noted in the README and the research note.

r1-34 (BA-E section; landside elevations of T1/T2/T3): PARTLY ALREADY FIXED; T3 part now FIXED.
- Already fixed in round 2: BA-E is drawn stepped in BD-02 (tapered edge over the clerestory, lower side roofs, glazed end wall), and BD-03 has the T1 Center and T2 landside elevations.
- Missing: Terminal 3. Added as BD-03 view 3, 1:400, developed along the SFO Museum outline edges that face the central garage:
  - Lengths (obs): T3 West 106.4 m (alternating 10.3 / 4.5 m bays), a 16.6 m AirTrain/garage connector gap, T3 East 122.5 m.
  - Heights: the published CDR levels shown as metres above T3 L1 (L2 4.88, L3 10.36, R2 14.48, T3W parapet 16.76, R3 21.34); the subtraction is inf and the project datum is not printed (unk).
  - T3 West facade: materials from CDR p.23 'East Facade Wall Sections' (ACM panels, fritted window wall, ACM spandrel). Band heights are proportions read from that rendered section, which prints no dimensions (inf, low).
  - T3 East: the landside facade is not described in any source found (unk). Its mechanical penthouse extent and ~20-24 m set-back come from NAIP 2024 profiles. The NAIP wall band and shadow give about 6-9 m above the roof (obs, low), matching R3 - R2 = 6.9 m; it is drawn to R3 (inf).
  - Not drawn: the T3W penthouses, whose positions and heights the CDR does not give (unk).
- Heights I did not measure are drawn as unk placeholders, as the finding asked.
- I viewed the CDR pages only as rendered reference images in the scratchpad; nothing from them is committed.

Visual QA: I looked at the regenerated BD-01, BD-02, BD-03 PNGs and the BD-01 NAIP overlay crops. Label overlaps and clipping found along the way (T1 curb text cut at the sheet edge, BA-E leader hiding the BA-B +19.04 label, T3 labels running off the sheet) are fixed.
